last_amend_reason:
ESC-017, amendment 17 — .swarm-loop/acceptance/test_e4_store_agent.py. GRANTED by Hank by explicit delegation ("the three things you were waiting on me for, I'll take your best judgment on"), ruled by the orchestrator, executed by a lane and verified by three independent readers.

THE DEFECT IN THE FROZEN SUITE: it ASSERTED THE PERMISSIVE SIDE of a security fail-open, so T-233 could not be closed by any lane. Measured against the unmodified door on the frozen suite's own payload helper: trust_snapshot OMITTED -> accepted=True reasons=(); trust_snapshot={} -> accepted=False reasons=('trust_snapshot_unavailable:store-external-1',); None -> accepted=True. And :1180 asserts accepted is True on exactly that call. Satisfying T-233 broke a frozen test; satisfying the frozen test kept the fail-open forever. Applying the T-233 fix against the unamended suite gave 7 failed / 13 passed, taking e4_store_agent_passing from 20 to 13. FOUR escape routes were implemented and measured dead (a sentinel for omitted-vs-None; a real eligibility registry, dead on data - store-external-1 exists in exactly one non-test file, a doc example; making explicit {} accept, which leaves everything green and STILL fails T-233's gate because that gate asserts a conjunction, and is a security regression besides; fixing in contracts.boundary, dead because the submission is identical both ways). A fifth was hunted for and not found. tickets.json is itself frozen, so even re-pointing T-233's gate would have been a frozen amendment: there was no do-nothing option.

WHAT CHANGED: 35 insertions, ZERO deletions, zero assertions touched. One helper deriving a populated trust snapshot from each payload's OWN store_id, plus one argument line in _present (the choke point for all 21 _accepts/_rejects calls) and one on the single direct receive_bid call. Two edit sites, not fourteen.

THE PROPOSED REMEDY IN MY OWN RULING WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. It said "pass an eligibility argument the way they already pass nonce_store=". The natural reading is the EMPTY mapping, and the empty mapping is the REFUSING case - measured, trust_snapshot={} flips every positive control red. An outside session that built it independently ALSO broke two controls on its first attempt by hardcoding a single store id, because two calls use store-external-2: that is T-233's own defect, a single-payload fix to a universal property, reproduced inside the fix for it. Three further countable claims in my ruling were refuted by readers: "eligibility" appears 0 times in the file (the parameter is trust_snapshot), trust_snapshot= was passed on 0 calls not 1, and blacklist= appears once not twice. The SUBSTANCE survived all of it - no accepting call passed an eligibility-shaped argument - which is what made the errors dangerous rather than obvious.

CONDITIONS, ALL MEASURED: count stays 120 and E4 stays 20, before and after, with real pytest (120 collected / 120 passed / E4 20). Both directions: amended suite vs UNMODIFIED door 120 passed; vs FIXED door 120 passed. Mutation sensitivity IDENTICAL mutant-for-mutant across eight probes (signature-check-off 9/9, key-trial 2/2, freshness-infinite 3/3, blacklist-ignored 5/5, nonce-no-op 3/3, enqueue-skipped 15/15, envelope-gate-off 0/0 surviving both because the signature covers the envelope). make verify OK: all, exit 0. store-agent 296 passed.

THE LANE WENT PAST ITS BRIEF WHERE MEASUREMENT SAID THE BRIEF WAS WRONG, and this is the most valuable part. My ruling required parametrizing T-233's probe over payload shapes. Measured: that blocks exactly ONE gaming key. Four others - keying on offer.expires_at, a store_id allowlist, auction_id, or nonce - leave the probe green with the fail-open ALIVE. It added a randomized property instead: trust_snapshot=None must be indistinguishable from {} in verdict AND reasons over 60 randomized bids, each armed with a real row first. It also found THREE sweeps that went QUIET rather than red (T-229 6->0 of 8, T-281 70->0 of 79, T-241 48->0 of 66) and gave each an arming assertion, and caught and fixed a regression it had introduced itself.

ONE PROPERTY IS DELIBERATELY LOST AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the frozen file previously pinned, by accident, "the door admits with no trust_snapshot supplied". Nothing asserts that now. That IS T-233's defect, so removing it is the point - but it is a real reduction in what the file constrains, not a no-op.

COST TO THE TRAJECTORY: the 120/120 measured at 7b5d1f0 and pushed at c3fc49a was achieved against the PRE-amendment suite. Any comparison across this boundary must say so. No metric, no target, no other frozen file, no product contract changed - the suite still collects 120 and E4 still counts 20.
